name: The example
why: 19. Every line carries between 0 and its capacity, and at stations 1 to 4 the flow in equals the flow out. 10 + 9 leave the source.

name: Over capacity
why: None. The last line, 4 → 5, has capacity 10 but carries 11.

name: Flow lost at a station
why: None. Station 4 takes in 6 + 9 = 15 but sends out 5 + 9 = 14. Every number is within its capacity, so only the conservation check catches this.

name: A negative flow
why: None. A flow is never below 0 on a line. Flow backwards would need a line the other way.

name: The empty flow
why: 0: nothing moves, and that is a valid flow.

name: Flow into the source
why: 2. The value is the flow out of the source minus the flow into it: 3 − 1. The sink receives 2, the same number.

name: A loop of flow
why: 5. The flow going round 1 → 2 → 1 keeps every rule; it simply adds nothing to the value.

name: Repeated lines and a line to itself
why: 4. Each line is checked on its own. A line from station 1 to itself adds 7 in and 7 out.

name: Wrong number of values
why: None: the flow must give one number per line.

name: 100,000 stations
show: 1,000 paths of flow, 1,000 loops of flow, 97,000 empty lines
why: 3997: the paths carry 1, 2, …, 7 in turn. Add up flow in and out for every station in one pass over the lines: O(V + E). Going through every line once for each station is O(V · E).

name: 100,000 stations, one wrong number
show: the same, with one line in the middle of a path carrying 1 more
why: None: two stations on path 777 break conservation, and the capacity rule still holds.
